title: Felix and the Confession
premise: Bram Iversen, an estate lawyer with a flawless record of closing every case she takes, is hired by a dying stranger named Felix to prove that a murder listed in a will hasn't happened yet — the will names its own future victim. The document points to Marlowe House, where a woman named Ada Corliss is scheduled to die on the anniversary of her sister's drowning, and where everyone from the housekeeper to the local constable insists the case was settled decades ago. As Bram digs through forged ledgers, suppressed confessions, and Felix's own tangled past as Ada's first love, she discovers the 'murder' is a ritual of memory: each year the household reenacts the sister's death to keep a guilty secret buried. When the anniversary arrives, Bram must choose between exposing the truth and letting Ada finally confess — and in the end it is not the law but a spoken confession, witnessed by Bram and sealed in a new will, that closes the case no court ever could.
about_author: Edmund Nystrom is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's final wishes before writing his own. He lives near the coast, where he collects old wills and insists that every one of them is a mystery waiting for the right reader.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Bram. A gaunt stranger named Felix pays Bram triple her fee in advance to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, sliding across her desk a will dated three days in the future. Bram, who has never refused a closed-and-paid case, accepts against her better judgment. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Marlowe House
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram travels to the rain-soaked coastal estate named in the will, finding a household frozen in time — dust sheets, stopped clocks, a portrait turned to face the wall. The housekeeper, Mrs. Pell, recognizes Felix's name and goes white. Emotional beat: dread arriving before any facts do.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears It Was Closed
chapters.summary: POV Bram. The local constable, Inspector Hale, tells Bram the drowning of Lila Corliss was ruled accidental thirty years ago and warns her off. But Hale's hands shake as he says it, and he refuses to look at the portrait wall. Emotional beat: the first crack in an official story.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram meets Ada Corliss, elegant and serene, who speaks of her drowned sister with unsettling tenderness and asks whether Felix sent her. She neither confirms nor denies anything, only says, 'Anniversaries matter in this house.' Emotional beat: fascination laced with fear.

chapters.title: Felix's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Searching Felix's rented room, Bram finds fifty years of ledger entries, each marking the same date, each entry shorter than the last — until this year's, which simply reads: 'Tell her, or I will.' Emotional beat: realizing Felix isn't a client but a participant.

chapters.title: The Drowned Sister
chapters.summary: POV Bram via records and interviews. Bram reconstructs Lila Corliss's death: a midnight swim, a missing boat, a coroner bribed into haste. Two witnesses from that night are still alive — one now mute, one recently dead. Emotional beat: grief for a girl the town chose to forget.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: POV Mrs. Pell. The housekeeper, unable to sleep, nearly tells Bram what she saw from the boathouse window thirty years ago, then stops herself at Ada's name. She gives Bram only a key instead. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with conscience.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Key
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Behind a false panel in the boathouse, Bram finds Lila's recovered belongings — never returned to the family — including a diary whose final pages have been razored out. Someone wanted the story cut short. Emotional beat: the thrill of evidence turning to horror at its absence.

chapters.title: Inspector Hale's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Hale. The inspector drinks alone and remembers taking money from old Mr. Corliss to close the file, telling himself it was mercy. Now Bram's questions have reopened everything, and someone has left him a copy of the mutilated diary page. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: What Felix Confessed
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram tracks Felix to a hospice, where he admits he was on the water the night Lila died — and that Ada's father made him choose between silence and ruin. He paid Bram not to prevent a murder but to witness a confession he's too cowardly to make himself. Emotional beat: pity replacing suspicion.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Ritual
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram learns the household reenacts Lila's last night every year — candles, a rowboat, a minute of darkness — a ritual Ada believes keeps her sister's spirit at peace. This year, Felix intends to attend. Emotional beat: understanding the murder is a ceremony, not a crime.

chapters.title: A Case That Can't Be Closed
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Bram confronts her own record: closing this case means destroying Ada's fragile peace or burying the truth forever. Her mentor's voice reminds her lawyers close cases; they don't heal them. Emotional beat: the professional creed cracking under moral weight.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: POV Ada. In her own chapters for the first time, Ada reveals she took the diary pages herself years ago — because they describe Lila planning to run away with Felix, and because they name who followed her to the boat. Emotional beat: love and duty strangling each other.

chapters.title: Hale Draws His Line
chapters.summary: POV Hale. Cornered by Bram with the bribery evidence, Hale offers a bargain: immunity for testimony. Bram realizes justice inside the law would take months — past the anniversary, past whatever Felix is planning. Emotional beat: the law revealed as too slow for the living.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: POV Bram. On the eve of the anniversary, Bram finds the razored diary pages hidden in Felix's coat: Lila wrote that her father followed her to the dock, that they argued, that she slipped. Old Corliss watched her drown and said nothing. Emotional beat: the truth arriving cold and complete.

chapters.title: The Reenactment
chapters.summary: POV Bram. At midnight the household gathers at the dock for the ritual. Felix appears, dying and determined, and begins to speak the confession he hired Bram to provoke. Ada begs him to stop; Hale watches from the shadows; the candles gutter. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Confession at the Waterline
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada silences Felix and confesses herself — not to the killing, but to thirty years of knowing, of curating the silence, of loving Felix and hating him for surviving when Lila didn't. She reads the restored pages aloud to the water. Emotional beat: catharsis bought at the price of everything.

chapters.title: What the Law Can Hold
chapters.summary: POV Bram. With Hale present, Bram formalizes the moment: Ada's statement taken down, Felix's affidavit signed, the old file reopened properly. No arrest follows — the guilty are dead — but the record finally tells the truth. Emotional beat: justice outside the law folded back into it.

chapters.title: Felix's Last Will
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Felix dies two days later, and Bram executes his true will: his estate funds a memorial for Lila and restores the mutilated diary, published whole. The case Bram was paid to prove hadn't happened ends as the one thing she couldn't have predicted — a gift. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: The Portrait Turned Back
chapters.summary: POV Mrs. Pell. The housekeeper turns Lila's portrait to face the room again and takes down the dust sheets, letting light into Marlowe House for the first time in decades. Ada watches from the stairs and, for the first time, cries. Emotional beat: a household exhaling after thirty years.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Back in her office, Bram writes the final report and breaks her streak deliberately: she marks the case 'closed — by confession,' a category that doesn't exist until she invents it. Hale sends a bottle of whisky with a note: 'Some cases close you.' Emotional beat: hard-won peace.

chapters.title: What Bram Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Months later, Bram visits Lila's memorial bench above the cove and leaves a copy of the published diary. She understands now why Felix chose her: not despite her perfect record, but because someone who always closes cases needed to learn which ones should stay open. Emotional beat: quiet transformation, love remembered against duty.
